top_categories.workout_context: Rule of Three's Tarmac, Ozark gravel and technical B-roads forces constant power changes. Surge over the rough stuff, settle on the smooth, repeat for 115 miles.
Race-pace efforts that mimic Rule of Three's demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before May.
At mile 60 of 115, glycogen is gone. This workout teaches your body to produce watts on fumes.
Rule of Three's relentless mixed-surface riding around Bentonville rewards steady threshold power. Surging and recovering costs more watts than just holding.
How long can you hold 105% FTP before you blow? At Rule of Three, that number decides whether you bridge or get dropped.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of Rule of Three. Train it until it feels boring.
When someone attacks on relentless mixed-surface riding around Bentonville, you have 10 seconds to respond or you're off the back. This builds that response.
At Rule of Three, surges push you above threshold and you have to recover while still riding. Over-unders train exactly that.
2-minute all-out efforts on relentless mixed-surface riding around Bentonville. Closing gaps, responding to attacks, sprinting for position. Train the burn.
Smooth pedaling at 115 miles saves muscle. Bad technique at mile 10 is invisible. At mile 80 it's a cramp.
Long rides with hard efforts mixed in. Simulates what Rule of Three's relentless mixed-surface riding around Bentonville actually does to you.
Every hard session works better with a bigger aerobic base. At 115 miles, base fitness is the difference between racing and surviving.

race_overlay.nutrition: Target 60–80g carbs/hour for Rule of Three’s 115 miles. Start fueling within the first 30 minutes — early fueling prevents late-race collapse. Bonking at mile 60 is a nutrition failure, not a fitness failure.
race_overlay.terrain: Highly technical terrain at Rule of Three demands practice on similar surfaces. Ride relentless mixed-surface riding around bentonville at race-day cadence weekly. Expect: tarmac, ozark gravel and technical b-roads, flowy, climby singletrack. Practice cornering, descending, and power delivery on unstable surfaces. Dial in tire pressure before race week — 5 PSI wrong costs you 15+ minutes over 115 miles.

pack_summary: This 10-workout pack focuses on Gravel Specific, Race Simulation, and Durability to prepare you for 115 miles of relentless mixed-surface riding around bentonville in Bentonville, Arkansas.
